problem: VLN agents are trained on only 61 Matterport3D scans and overfit to them. Prior environment augmentations (EnvDrop feature dropout, REM mixup, EnvEdit style editing) only re-style existing MP3D scenes and add no new objects or layouts. Adding HM3D scans (HM3D-AutoVLN) still depends on expensive manually captured 3D environments, so it cannot scale further.
motivation: Diverse photorealistic indoor environments with human-height viewpoints are costly to collect, while text-to-image diffusion models can synthesize unlimited, varied room imagery. Conditioning generation on captions of the real MP3D views keeps object co-occurrence plausible (a bedroom gets a bed and dresser, not a fridge) while changing appearance and layout. Recursive outpainting avoids the inconsistency of stitching independently generated views, which would confuse spatial reasoning.
key_idea: Caption each of the 36 discretized views of every R2R training panorama with BLIP-2, generate a new view with Stable Diffusion, then outpaint recursively (rotating right/up/down, conditioned on neighbouring captions) into a coherent new 360° panorama. These panoramas feed VLN training in two ways: mPLUG-speaker instruction data for pre-training, and random observation replacement during fine-tuning.
insight: Text-conditioned generated panoramas act as semantically aligned but visually and layout-novel augmentation: partially swapping them into real trajectories regularizes the agent without breaking instruction–observation alignment, provided the swap ratio is moderate. On R2R val-unseen, replacing 30% of viewpoints gives the best SR (74.41 vs 72.84 at 0%). Larger ratios misalign trajectories with instructions: ratio 0.7 gives SR 72.33. Gains grow with the number of generated scans: SPL is 62.48 / 62.88 / 63.88 / 64.27 for 10 / 30 / 61 / 122 scans, not yet saturated. However, 10 scans alone falls below the 63.37 baseline. Speaker-data pre-training helps most on under-specified dialog instructions: CVDN GP rises from 5.50 to 5.93 on val and reaches 7.17 on test. The mPLUG-based speaker beats the EnvDrop LSTM speaker on SR and GP but not on R2R SPL.
method: Room description collection: every one of the 36 discretized views of each panorama in the 61 R2R training scans is captioned with BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL, giving fine-grained per-view descriptions that keep realistic object co-occurrence.

Text-conditioned recursive outpainting: a zero-elevation view is first generated from its caption with stable-diffusion-v2.1-base. The image is then shifted right/up/down by p_r%/p_u%/p_d% and the unseen region is outpainted with stable-diffusion-v1.5-inpainting, conditioned on the neighbouring view's caption. This repeats until all 36 views exist and can be stitched into a consistent panorama. Output: 7,644 panoramas from 275,184 images, about 2 days on 6 A100s.

mPLUG speaker for generated environments: mPLUG-base (350M) is fine-tuned on R2R. Each trajectory is represented by the agent-facing single view per step, encoded with CLIP-ViT-B/16 and flattened into patch tokens. The speaker re-labels all R2R training paths rendered with PanoGen observations, giving 4,675 instruction–trajectory pairs.

Pre-training: the DUET agent (CLIP-ViT-B/16 features) is pre-trained on R2R + PREVALENT + PanoGen speaker data with MLM, ITM (4 negatives, 2 of them shuffled trajectories) and SAP; 150k iterations at batch size 64.

Fine-tuning with panorama replacement: DUET-style pseudo-interactive-demonstration fine-tuning in which m% (best 30%) of trajectory observations are randomly replaced by the corresponding PanoGen panorama; 40k iterations at batch size 8. The final R2R model uses 2 generated panoramas per original (122 'scans').

setting.backbone: DUET dual-scale graph transformer trained on CLIP-ViT-B/16 visual features. Data-generation tools: BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL and Stable Diffusion v2.1-base / v1.5-inpainting (frozen), plus an mPLUG-base speaker (fine-tuned).
setting.model_size: speaker mPLUG-base 350M; DUET agent size not stated
setting.training_data: Pre-training: R2R + PREVALENT augmented data + 4,675 mPLUG-speaker instruction–trajectory pairs in PanoGen environments. Fine-tuning: R2R / R4R / CVDN train splits with observations randomly replaced by PanoGen panoramas; 7,644 generated panoramas covering the 61 train scans, doubled to 122 'scans' for the best R2R model. No new human annotation.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views, CLIP-ViT-B/16 features) + navigation history/graph
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (DUET: adjacent or observed-but-unvisited global nodes, plus STOP)

numbers_note: The 'PanoGen' row in Table 1 is two different models. On R2R it is the panorama-replacement fine-tuning model with 122 generated scans (val-unseen numbers equal Table 5 row 5). On CVDN it is the mPLUG speaker pre-training model (val GP 5.93 equals the Table 2 row). R4R appears only in ablation Tables 2/3, not the main table. The R2R test SPL gain is inconsistent: the abstract/intro claim +1.9% SPL (vs SE3DS 60.0), while Sec. 6.1 claims +2.9% SPL over DUET (61.9 vs 59.0). Checkpoints were selected on val-unseen, and results are single runs with no variance reported.
results: Learning with PanoGen environments reports new SotA on the R2R test leaderboard at the time: SR 71.7 / SPL 61.9, vs DUET 69.0 / 59.0 and SE3DS 66.0 / 60.0. On R2R val-unseen the full model reaches SR 74.2 / SPL 64.3, vs the reproduced DUET-CLIP baseline 72.84 / 63.37. The largest gain is on CVDN test: GP 7.17 vs HAMT 5.58, +1.59 m or 28.5% relative, from speaker pre-training. On R4R val-unseen, replacement fine-tuning raises SPL from 41.94 to 44.25.
limitations: Each generated panorama is produced independently per viewpoint on the original navigation graph, with no depth or 3D geometry. Adjacent viewpoints in a trajectory are not mutually consistent, and the method cannot be used directly for continuous-environment VLN. There is also no quantitative navigation ablation of recursive outpainting versus disjoint per-view generation; the comparison is only qualitative.

Gains on R2R/R4R val-unseen are modest (about 1-1.6 SR) and mixed. mPLUG speaker pre-training lowers R2R SPL (62.81 vs 63.37) and R4R SR (45.78 vs 46.61). Using only 10 generated scans also underperforms the baseline in SPL. Single runs with checkpoint selection on val-unseen.
Stated by the authors: Stable Diffusion inpainting is used zero-shot (trained on LAION-aesthetics), not fine-tuned on room images; only VLN tasks are evaluated.
